page: UpCloud GPU-32xCPU-160GB-2xRTXPRO6000 is a GPU-accelerated server running on a KVM hypervisor. It is powered by an x86_64 AMD EPYC 9555 processor configured with 32 physical cores and 32 vCPUs under a shared allocation model. The system features 160.0 GB of system memory, providing 5.0 GB per core, and is equipped with two NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition GPUs that deliver a combined 191 GB of VRAM. Local storage is not bundled with this instance type, and it includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

In benchmark testing, this server demonstrates top-tier performance across computational and memory-bound tasks. The system achieved a Geekbench single-core score of 2686.0 and a multi-core score of 24576.0. Memory bandwidth is highly efficient, with large-block read speeds reaching 455.64 GB/sec and write speeds at 228.66 GB/sec. For artificial intelligence workloads, the dual-GPU setup delivers exceptional LLM inference speeds, processing 8118.49 tokens/sec for prompts and generating 221.74 tokens/sec on a medium 7B model.

Given its hardware profile, this server offers high qualitative cost efficiency for parallel computing and deep learning workloads. The shared CPU allocation is a notable tradeoff for sustained, pure CPU-bound tasks, but the massive GPU memory and high memory bandwidth mitigate this for accelerated workloads. It is highly recommended for machine learning inference, ray tracing, image processing, and complex physics simulations.
